findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

Observed multiple items in the walk-in cooler to lack appropriate date marking. Cook stated that the employees forgot to date mark the items the day before. He date marked all the items. Observed multiple foods cooling in the walk in cooler with no time stamp on the items (sausage links, noodles, soup). Food MUST be time stamped and a date shall be put on them to ensure proper cooling. It is recommended to start food time and temperature logs.
750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed ready to eat foods with no date mark in the walk in cooler. Make sure to date mark foods within 24hours of preparing and used or discarded within 7 days.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the ate or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
1) (REPEAT) Observed foods in the walk in freezer stored on the floor. Foods must be at least 6" off the floor. 2) Observed foods uncovered in the walk in freezer. Make sure to properly protect the food during storage.
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.
750-130(b) Food shall be stored at least 6 inches off the floor.  Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.comment:
Observed a cook cut lettuce and assemble a sandwich with bare hand contact. Gloves must be worn when handling ready to eat foods.
750-160 Ready to eat foods shall be handled in a manner to minimize direct hand contact.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
Observed no sanitizer in the sanitizer bucket. The owner stated they place a little bit of detergent and a little sanitizer in the bucket. Make sure to make two separate buckets and put detergent in one and sanitizer in the other.
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
1) Observed the coffee spout on the coffee machine to be soiled. Clean the spout. 2) Observed the microwave to be soiled. Clean the microwave so that food does not drip onto the food.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
1) Observed single service items (straws, napkins) stored on the floor in the dry storage area. Move single service items at least 6" off the floor. 2) Observed coffee filters unprotected in the server station. Make sure to protect single service items at all times.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water disposed properly
findings.comment:
Observed waste water in a bucket in the mop room. The waste water was disposed of properly. Make sure to discard waste water after each use.
750-1050 All water containing sewage shall be disposed of  properly either by a public sewage system or an approved private disposal system which is constructed and operated in conformance with applicable State and local laws, ordinances and regulations.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
Observed a leak at the three compartment sink. Repair the leak.
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
Observed no paper towels at the handsink on the cookline. Replace the paper towel dispenser.
750-1120e A supply of soap and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.comment:
Observed the back door to have a small gap at the bottom. The owner stated that there is a work order in to get the door fixed. Will spot check in thirty days to check the back door.
750-1170 Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed the handsink to be coming apart from the wall in the server station. Recaulk the handsink to the wall.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed soup in the walk in cooler with no time mark. When cooling items, a time must be marked on the product to ensure proper cooling.
750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed shell eggs that were stored at room temperature and just placed in the walk in cooler. One egg was probed and was 70F. Store flats of eggs in cold holding as long as possible.
750-153(a) Food shall not be held more that 4 hours past the point it is removed from temperature control. Do not hold food in excess of four hours after removal from temperature control.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed marinara sauce and ham that was stored under raw beef in the walk in cooler. The items were moved to a different shelf to correct the violation.
750-130(d) All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
CORRECTED: 1). Observed a box of hash browns on the floor in the walk-in cooler across from the three compartment sink. All food should be 6inches above from the floor. CORRECTED: 2). Observed uncovered food in the walk-in freezer. Provide cover on food in the walk-in freezer.
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.
750-130(b) Food shall be stored at least 6 inches off the floor.  Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
CORRECTED: Observed the ice scoop handle not extending out of the ice in the ice bin in the waitress area. Place ice scoop handle extending out of the ice.
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment:
CORRECTED: Observed an employee drink in the bottom salad prep cooler without a lid. All employee drinks need to have a lid and straw and placed in a designated area. The employee drink was discarded and moved during the time of inspection.
750-530a Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed the plastic ice scoop to be cracked in the ice machine maker.  Replace ice scoop in the ice machine maker.
750-650a Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored

750-140(b)  Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 140°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours.

Observed a large container of bacon stored underneath a fly strip in the kitchen.  Fly strips cannot be used in food preparation areas.  The area the bacon was located in was previously stated as not a food prep area.  If this part is a food preparation area, smooth and easily cleanable ceiling tiles must be installed. Do not store any foods in this area.

Proper storage methods were discussed at the inspection and handouts were given. Properly store foods at all times.

750-130(d) All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods.
